root_cause.text: In `drivers/xen/sys-hypervisor.c`’s `buildid_show()` sysfs handler, the Xen build-id returned by `HYPERVISOR_xen_version(XENVER_build_id)` was treated as a NUL-terminated string and passed to `sprintf("%s")`, causing an out-of-bounds read/copy overflow when the binary build-id lacked a terminating NUL.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes “The build id … is neither NUL terminated nor a string” and replaces `sprintf(buffer, "%s", buildid->buf);` with `memcpy(buffer, buildid->buf, ret);` while adding the comment “Build id is binary, not a string.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a size guard in `buildid_show()` to reject build-id output that exceeds `PAGE_SIZE`.
intent_record.what: A new check was added after obtaining `ret` from the earlier logic: if `ret > PAGE_SIZE`, the function now immediately returns `-ENOSPC` before calling `kmalloc(sizeof(*buildid) + ret, GFP_KERNEL)`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from attempting to allocate a build-id buffer larger than a page-backed sysfs buffer can safely accommodate, avoiding oversized allocation/copy handling and failing early with an out-of-space error instead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix build ID sysfs output to copy binary data directly instead of formatting it as a C string.
intent_record.what: In buildid_show(), the code that handled a successful HYPERVISOR_xen_version(XENVER_build_id, buildid) call was changed from sprintf(buffer, "%s", buildid->buf) to memcpy(buffer, buildid->buf, ret), and a comment was added stating that the build id is binary, not a string.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now copies the exact number of bytes returned by the hypervisor instead of treating the build ID as a NUL-terminated string. This prevents incorrect string formatting and preserves binary data integrity when exposing the build ID through sysfs.

It fetches the build-id length with `ret = HYPERVISOR_xen_version(XENVER_build_id, NULL);`, allocates `kmalloc(sizeof(*buildid) + ret, GFP_KERNEL);`, then fills the buffer and finally does `ret = sprintf(buffer, "%s", buildid->buf);`. This treats `buildid->buf` as a NUL-terminated string, even though the root cause states the Xen build-id is binary data and may lack a terminating NUL, leading to out-of-bounds read/copy overflow.
